q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
# NVIDIA Q2 FY2027 Forward Guidance Analysis

## (a) Time left until resolution

Today is 2026-08-11. Q2 FY2027 guidance was provided on 2026-05-20 (as stated in the research). The question asks "What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release?" 

This is ambiguous - it could mean:
1. What was the guidance provided during the Q1 FY2027 earnings call (already happened on 2026-05-20)?
2. What will the guidance be when Q2 FY2027 results are announced (future event)?

Given the phrasing "What will be" (future tense), I interpret this as asking for the guidance that will be issued at the Q2 FY2027 earnings release itself, which typically occurs ~2-3 months after quarter end. Q2 FY2027 would end in August 2026, so earnings would be released in late August or early September 2026.

**Time remaining: ~3-4 weeks until Q2 FY2027 earnings announcement**

However, the research provides NVIDIA's Q2 FY2027 guidance already issued on May 20, 2026: **$91.0 billion ± 2%** (range: $89.18B - $92.82B).

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

The most likely outcome is that NVIDIA will maintain or slightly adjust its $91.0B guidance when announcing Q2 FY2027 results. The research shows:

- Q1 FY2027 actual revenue: $81.6B
- Q2 FY2027 forward guidance: $91.0B ± 2% ($89.18B - $92.82B)

This represents a ~11.5% sequential growth from Q1 to Q2. Companies typically maintain or slightly modify guidance in the final month before a quarter ends, but major revisions are less common unless significant business changes occur.

The guidance is notably conservative in that it **excludes all Data Center revenue from China**, which suggests management is being prudent given geopolitical uncertainty.

## (c) What would push the value lower?

- **Deteriorating demand signals** in the final weeks of Q2 (late August)
- **Geopolitical developments** restricting Chinese customer revenue more than expected
- **Competitive pressure** from AMD or other AI accelerator vendors
- **Inventory corrections** in the channel
- **Broader economic slowdown** impacting enterprise cloud spending
- **Manufacturing constraints** on H100/H200 production

## (d) What would push the value higher?

- **Stronger-than-expected demand** from cloud providers (Meta, Google, Microsoft, OpenAI customers)
- **Surprise upside** in automotive or consumer segments
- **Unexpected China revenue** becoming possible if geopolitical situation improves (though currently excluded)
- **Market share gains** from competitors accelerating AI adoption
- **New product launches** driving incremental demand (Blackwell ramp-up)

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

From the research provided:
- Q1 FY2027 revenue: $81.6B (actual)
- Q2 FY2027 guidance: $91.0B ± 2% (issued May 20, 2026)
- This guidance was issued ~2 months into the quarter
- Sequential growth rate implied: ~11.5%

No reliable historical base rate for how often NVIDIA adjusts forward guidance within weeks of release is provided in the materials.

## Analysis

The core fact is that **the guidance has already been provided**: $91.0 billion ± 2%, which translates to a range of $89.18B to $92.82B. 

Given that:
1. This guidance was issued relatively recently (May 20, 2026)
2. We are now in early-to-mid August 2026, with only ~3-4 weeks until Q2 ends
3. NVIDIA rarely makes dramatic guidance revisions this late in a quarter
4. The guidance was explicitly stated with a specific number and ±2% band
5. Management stated it conservatively (no China DC revenue included)

The most probable outcome is that the actual guidance issued at Q2 earnings will be **within or very close to the $89.18B-$92.82B range already provided**, with the central estimate most likely near $91.0B.

For a point estimate within the broader question range (99.5B-115.5B):
- The provided guidance of $91.0B ± 2% sits at the lower end of the stated range
- This is the most concrete, defensible estimate
- There's modest upside risk if demand is strong
- There's modest downside risk if there are channel corrections

**My point estimate:** $91.0 billion (the midpoint of the already-issued guidance)

With credible interval accounting for:
- 10th percentile (potential downside): $88.5 billion
- 50th percentile (most likely): $91.0 billion  
- 90th percentile (upside scenario): $93.5 billion

q_45367.research_text:
NVIDIA's forward guidance for Q2 FY2027 revenue was released on May 20, 2026, as part of its Q1 FY2027 earnings report. The company expects revenue to be $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2% [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027.html), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm), [nvidianews.nvidia.com](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-first-quarter-fiscal-2027). This projection is significantly higher than the average quarterly revenue estimate of $86.84 billion from LSEG analysts [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027.html). Notably, NVIDIA's outlook does not assume any Data Center compute revenue from China [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027.html), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm).

For Q1 FY2027, NVIDIA reported record revenue of $81.6 billion, an 85% increase from the previous year, with Data Center revenue reaching $75.2 billion, up 92% year-over-year [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm), [barchart.com](https://www.barchart.com/story/news/3449043/what-to-expect-from-nvidia-s-q2-2027-earnings-report). The company also announced an increase in its quarterly cash dividend from $0.01 to $0.25 per share [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm).

- This implies a range of 74.4% to 75.4%

The most likely outcome is that the actual reported GAAP gross margin will fall within this guided range, centered near 74.9%. This is typical corporate behavior — companies guide conservatively and usually hit or slightly beat their guidance.

Given that:
1. The guidance was just issued ~2.5 months ago (May 2026)
2. It includes a ±50 bps buffer for uncertainty
3. No major operational disruptions have been mentioned in the research

The most probable outcome is **74.9% ± some modest variance within the guided range**, likely between 74.5% and 75.2%.

**(c) What would push the value lower?**

**(d) What would push the value higher?**

- Better-than-expected product mix (higher-margin products outperforming)
- Manufacturing efficiency gains and favorable yield improvements

- Favorable foreign exchange impacts
- Lower-than-expected costs or better supply negotiations

**(e) Base rate or historical reference values**

The research explicitly states that NVIDIA's Q1 FY2027 actual GAAP gross margin was **74.9%**, which exactly matches their Q2 FY2027 guidance point estimate of 74.9%. This is a strong anchor.

Historically, NVIDIA has been reasonably accurate with gross margin guidance (±50 bps bands), typically hitting within or very close to their stated ranges.

---

# Probability Distribution Reasoning

The range provided is 72.95% to 76.05%, which is notably wider than NVIDIA's stated guidance range of 74.4% to 75.4%.

Given:

- Time to resolution is minimal (~2-4 weeks), limiting major surprises

The distribution should be:
- **Concentrated tightly around 74.9%** (center of guidance)
- **Roughly symmetric within the 74.4%-75.4% band**
- **Much lower probability in the tails outside this band**
- **Non-zero but modest tail risk below 74.4% or above 75.4%**

For the full range (72.95% to 76.05%):
- Values below 74.0% or above 76.0% are unlikely but possible (macro shocks, guidance misses)
- Most probability mass is 74.2% to 75.6%

---

Median (50th percentile): 74.90
